ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows isotherms in a certain sea area; there is a curved isotherm above, labeled 18℃ on the right; below there is also a curved isotherm, labeled 17℃ on the right. On the left side of the figure near the middle, near the label a, there is a small-range closed isotherm, and inside the closed circle it is labeled 17℃. It differs from the shape of the surrounding larger-range isotherms and appears as a local closed anomaly. Then reason: The question stem limits it to "a certain sea area". If place a were only an ordinary continuous seawater area, the isotherms usually should be continuously distributed with the surrounding seawater; but a local closed isotherm appears at place a, indicating that there may be local land affecting the distribution of sea-surface temperature there, causing the isotherm to close abnormally. Therefore, area a may be an island in the sea.
